transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-07 14:00 PT | Duration: 54 minutes | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Sarah Patel (CTO, Spectral Health), Tom O'Neill (Infra Lead), Mary Alvarez (Procurement), Diego Ramos (ML Engineer)

Summary section (auto): Spectral Health is leaning toward a 12-month renewal with a committed capacity uplift and APAC region enablement. They requested updated pricing and a benchmarking run to validate latency and cost under their prompt mix. Security review (SOC2, VPC) is gating private peering timeline.

00:00 Maya: okay, welcome everyone, thanks for joining. quick check, is everyone on from Spectral?
00:06 Sarah: yep hi, Sarah here, thanks for doing this. we've got Tom and Mary and Diego on the call.
00:10 Maya: great. objective today is to align on renewal options, scope the APAC add, and make sure we have the next technical steps for the bench and security review.
00:18 Ethan: hi all, i'll be the SE on the bench, want to understand your traffic patterns and latency s l a goals.
00:25 Tom: baseline for EU has been pretty solid with your hosted service, average p95 token latency around 280 to 320ms but that's with caching on our side. APAC has been a pain, we see 800ms plus to the hosted endpoint from singapore.
00:40 Sarah: correct, and with the 2027 product roadmap we need APAC latency closer to 250-350ms p95.
00:47 Diego: also the prompt mix is heavier — lots of long context, reranking calls, so throughput matters not just raw latency.
01:00 Ethan: got it. that'll influence whether we recommend a dedicated pool vs region pin for hosted. quick question: do you plan to move tokens for PHI? any new compliance constraints?
01:12 Sarah: we're not moving PHI to third-party hosted yet; for production scoring we need private VPC option. but for inference on non-sensitive models maybe hosted is fine. SOC 2 attestation is table-stakes for procurement.
01:24 Maya: understood, we can support a private deployment with a VPC peering and bring-your-own-kms for the private option. for hosted + apac we can enable region routing to ap-northeast and ap-southeast, but we'd need to size committed capacity to keep costs predictable.
01:41 Tom: what's your typical lead time to spin up APAC region dedicated capacity?
01:45 Ethan: for dedicated pools it's about 3-4 weeks after signed commitment and initial onboarding; for hosted region enable it's immediate but throughput is shared and we recommend a committed cap for guaranteed throughput.
01:58 Mary: procurement question, if we sign a 12-month with committed monthly units, is there flexibility to increase mid-term?
02:05 Maya: yes, we offer top-ups and mid-term amendments. there's also burst credits for spiky traffic but the unit price differs. we'll show scenarios in the quote.
02:12 Sarah: cost vs latency tradeoff — we'd like a recommendation. would dedicated give us consistent p95 under 350ms in APAC?
02:20 Ethan: likely yes for most models, but it depends on model selection and quantization. we can map your workload to a model variant and run a 24-hour bench to validate p95 and throughput.
02:34 Diego: can you simulate our reranking pipeline? we call the model for candidate scoring a lot; batching matters.
02:40 Ethan: absolutely, bring the prompt set and we'll mirror the batching/kv-cache characteristics. small note — transcription: "K-V" sometimes shows as "kay vee" in logs, but we understand.
02:49 Tom: (laughs) yeah the transcript generator is weird.
02:52 Mary: for security we need SOC2 Type II report, network diagram, and an audit log retention policy. also SSO/SAML and RBAC details.
03:03 Maya: we'll provide SOC2, a redacted network diag for VPC peering, and RBAC docs. audit logs are available — retention is configurable as an add-on.
03:12 Sarah: about data residency: EU data must remain in EU for certain workflows, but APAC users can hit APAC region. can Redwood route requests by customer tag or token?
03:22 Ethan: yes, routing policies can be token-level; you can pin specific routes or models to regions. we can show policy config in the console demo if helpful.
03:32 Tom: technical blocker — our current firewall rules limit egress ports, and we need to validate peering with your control plane. what's the handshake for peering?
03:40 Maya: we'll share the peering checklist and IP ranges. typically we use VPC peering or private link depending on the cloud provider — we'll include both options.
03:47 Diego: any thought on on-prem vs private cloud for long-term?
03:50 Ethan: if you want air-gapped or on-prem, that is a private deployment with an enterprise contract; that takes longer (6-8 weeks) and has additional ops cost. for now given your timeline, we recommend hosted with VPC peering for sensitive models and a dedicated pool in APAC.
04:08 Sarah: timeline — we want the new capacity live by mid-october to coincide with our release. procurement-wise, can we aim to sign the amendment by end of september?
04:18 Mary: that's our target, yes — we need the quote and legal terms to review.
04:22 Maya: we'll target to get the quote to you by 2026-09-10, and SE bench results by 2026-09-14.
04:29 Tom: for the bench, are you going to host a test harness or do we run it on our side?
04:32 Ethan: we'll run on Redwood side and mirror your prompts; alternatively we can provide a harness and run it from your environment depending on what network characteristics you want us to see. both options okay.
04:42 Diego: prefer Redwood-run so we control model backend but please simulate our client-side region ingress.
04:48 Ethan: noted. we'll run geo-distributed load from EU and APAC nodes to emulate your user population.
04:54 Sarah: one more thing — what happens if we exceed committed capacity? auto-fallback to hosted best-effort?
04:58 Maya: yes, we have a fallback policy that routes to a compatible model variant or to the shared hosted pool; you can configure soft throttles or hard caps. we'll include recommended policies in the doc.
05:10 Mary: contract language — we need an SLA clause for p95 latency in EU for critical routes. can we get a targeted SLA?
05:18 Maya: for dedicated pools we offer SLA-backed latency targets; for hosted it's best-effort with performance profiles. we'll outline the SLA options and what they require operationally.
05:27 Sarah: ok good. also curious about telemetry — token-level cost breakdown and per-route tracing. we rely heavily on observability.
05:34 Ethan: Redwood Console provides per-route token cost, latency breakdown and traces; we can export traces to your Datadog or internal tracing. we'll include sample screenshots.
05:44 Tom: competitors — we've run a quick PoC with CloudX and they struggled with long-context costs. any quantization recommendations to lower unit costs?
05:52 Ethan: yes, for reranking models we often recommend int8 or q4_0 quantization for throughput; we'll produce model-specific recommendations in the bench report.
06:02 Sarah: procurement question again — do you support purchase orders and net-30?
06:06 Mary: (adds) and what's the billing cadence if we do committed monthly units?
06:09 Maya: we support PO + net-30 for enterprise, billing on monthly cycles for committed capacity. annual prepay options available with discount.
06:17 Mary: ok that's good.
06:20 Maya: to recap, action items: i'll send the renewal quote w/ scenarios by 9/10; ethan will run bench and share by 9/14; tom to share network diagram and prompt set by 9/9; mary to confirm procurement dates by 9/16. any other outstanding?
06:34 Sarah: sounds good. oh and please include sample JSON for routing policies.
06:38 Ethan: will do, we'll paste examples and a short how-to in the doc.
06:42 Diego: small note — please include the model version mapping you plan to use for the bench so we can review for accuracy.
06:47 Ethan: yep, will include model variants and quantization profile mapping.
06:50 Maya: perfect, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the materials.
06:54 Mary: thanks, bye.
06:56 Sarah: thanks all. bye.
